title: Skill Sheet: Cardiac Arrest Management / AED
body:
## Before you read the checklist

The national EMT psychomotor exam ended in 2023; skills are now verified **in course** by your program against these same NREMT sheets, and states including NJ accept that verification.

> **Key:** Every line is `1 point`; the sheet totals in the low teens. There is no overall clock, but there is a hard one inside the station: the pulse/rhythm check must take under `10 seconds` and hands-off time around a shock must stay minimal.

## The order an evaluator scores it

### 1. Arrival and taking over CPR

1. Takes or verbalizes appropriate PPE precautions — `1`
2. Briefly questions the rescuer about arrest events, downtime, and care already given — `1`
3. Directs the rescuer to stop CPR — `1`
4. Verifies absence of spontaneous pulse (checks carotid for no more than `10 seconds`) — `1`
5. Directs resumption of CPR while the AED is readied — `1`

### 2. Attaching and using the AED

6. Turns on the defibrillator power — `1`
7. Attaches the AED to the patient (pads to bare, dry chest: right upper sternal border, left mid-axillary below the nipple) — `1`
8. Directs rescuer to stop CPR and ensures all individuals are clear of the patient — `1`
9. Initiates analysis of the rhythm — `1`
10. Delivers the shock, again ensuring everyone is clear — `1`
11. Immediately directs resumption of CPR, starting with compressions — `1`

### 3. After two minutes of CPR

12. Gathers additional information about the arrest event during the `2-minute` cycle — `1`
13. Confirms effectiveness of CPR (depth `2–2.4 in`, rate `100–120/min`, full recoil, ratio `30:2`) — `1`
14. After `2 minutes`, directs a stop to CPR, ensures all are clear, and re-initiates analysis — `1`
15. Directs insertion of an airway adjunct and ventilation with high-flow oxygen — `1`
16. Directs transport of the patient — `1`

> **Trap:** "No shock advised" does not mean stop. It means immediately resume compressions for another `2 minutes`, not stand there looking at the screen.

## Critical criteria (automatic fail)

- Failure to take or verbalize appropriate PPE precautions
- Failure to evaluate and find conditions of actual cardiac arrest before turning on the AED
- Failure to immediately deliver a shock when indicated
- Failure to immediately resume compressions after a shock or a "no shock advised"
- Interrupts CPR for more than `10 seconds` at any point other than the analysis/shock sequence
- Failure to correctly attach the AED to the patient
- Failure to operate the AED properly (inability to deliver a shock)
- Failure to ensure that all individuals are clear of the patient before analyzing the rhythm and before delivering each shock
- Failure to ensure that the patient is ventilated properly
- Failure to provide high-concentration oxygen
- Failure to check the patient's pulse for no more than `10 seconds`
- Uses or orders a dangerous or inappropriate intervention
- Exhibits unacceptable affect with the patient or other personnel

## How to narrate it out loud

- **Question and work at the same time.** "How long has he been down? Any bystander CPR?" while your hands are opening the AED case.
- **Say the pulse check out loud with its clock.** "Stop CPR — checking carotid — one, two, three... no pulse, resume compressions." Under `10 seconds` and everyone heard it.
- **Clear the patient in the loudest voice you own, three times.** "I'm clear, you're clear, everybody clear" — do a visual sweep before analyze and again before shock. Failing to clear is one of the easiest auto-fails to earn.
- **Shock then compress, in one breath.** "Shock delivered — resume compressions now." Never pause to reassess a pulse right after a shock.
- **Coach CPR quality by number.** "Rate is a little slow, bring it up to `110`, full recoil, switch compressors at `2 minutes`."
- **Direct the airway, do not do it yourself.** "Insert an OPA and bag with `15 L/min`, `30:2`, do not over-ventilate." You are running the code.

> **On shift:** The graded behaviors here are the same ones a hospital code team audits: chest-compression fraction, hands-off time under `10 seconds`, compressor swaps every `2 minutes`. Learn it on the manikin and you already know your job at a real code.
